label: Bible Study
prompt: For this is the _____ that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.
verse: For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.
note: The oldest message in the church — love one another, heard from the beginning.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: I will go before thee, and make the crooked places _____: I will break in pieces the gates of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron:
verse: I will go before thee, and make the crooked places straight: I will break in pieces the gates of brass, and cut in sunder the bars of iron:
note: Spoken to Cyrus: God goes on ahead, straightening crooked places and breaking gates of brass.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the _____. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
verse: And Boaz said unto her, At mealtime come thou hither, and eat of the bread, and dip thy morsel in the vinegar. And she sat beside the reapers: and he reached her parched corn, and she did eat, and was sufficed, and left.
note: Lunch with Boaz: bread dipped in vinegar and parched corn — Ruth ate her fill and had leftovers to take home.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Dead _____ cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
verse: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
note: A few dead flies can spoil a whole jar of perfume — and a little folly, a big reputation.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of _____: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
verse: His glory is like the firstling of his bullock, and his horns are like the horns of unicorns: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.
note: Yes, the KJV has 'unicorns' — Moses' blessing on Joseph's mighty horns. Most modern versions say 'wild ox.'
